title: Teenager Arrested in Connection to Tragic Mass Shooting Near FAMU Homecoming Game
snippet: A 15-year-old boy faces 11 counts of attempted homicide after a dispute near Bragg Stadium escalated into a mass shooting that injured 12 people.
content:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — A 15-year-old boy has been taken into custody in connection with a mass shooting outside Bragg Stadium that left 12 people injured following Florida A&M University's homecoming football game, police announced.

Tallahassee Police Department officers arrested Anthony Rivers III on Sunday, Oct. 25. He faces 11 counts of attempted homicide and one count of firearm possession by a delinquent. The tragedy marks one of the violent incidents in the city's history.

A Celebration Cut Short by Violence

According to TPD Police Chief Lawrence Revell, the shooting erupted from a physical altercation between individuals who knew one another. Investigators believe none of the victims struck by gunfire were the intended targets.

“What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families,” Revell said during a news conference.

Of the 12 total people injured, 11 suffered gunshot wounds, while a grandmother sustained injuries during the ensuing panic. Six of the victims were minors, including an 11-year-old child. As of Monday, six victims remain hospitalized, with one person in critical condition.

Investigation Remains Open for Potential Co-Conspirators

While Rivers was taken into custody after police worked around the clock, authorities cautioned that the investigation is far from over and additional arrests remain possible.

Detectives credited an outpouring of community support, tips, and digital evidence for helping identify the suspect. Police are continuing to urge anyone with cellphone footage or information regarding the incident to contact the TPD dedicated tip line at 850-891-4610 or submit evidence through their online community portal.
